name: Bark
description: A Bark bitcoin wallet on the Ark protocol: Ark, Lightning and on-chain payments.
primer:
Ark is the protocol this wallet runs on: a second layer on bitcoin for instant, cheap, self-custodial payments.
A VTXO is a coin on Ark: your Ark balance is made of VTXOs, and each one has a limited lifetime.
Boarding moves on-chain bitcoin into Ark; it becomes spendable once the board transaction confirms.
An arkoor payment is an instant Ark-to-Ark payment, made without waiting for a round.
A refresh swaps VTXOs for new ones in a round before they expire; the wallet usually does it for you.
VTXOs expire, after 28 days on Second's server, so they have to be refreshed or spent before then.
Offboarding is the normal way out: the Ark server cooperates and pays the amount to an on-chain address.
An emergency exit takes bitcoin on-chain without the server's help: slow and paid for in on-chain fees, but always possible.
transcriptionPrompt: A conversation about a Bark bitcoin wallet on the Ark protocol, by Second: VTXO, arkoor, boarding, offboarding, refresh, round, emergency exit, forfeit, connector, hArk, Pay2Anchor, barkd, captaind, Swaptopia, Lightning, BOLT11, LNURL, zap, Nostr, sats, on-chain, signet, Esplora.

terms.summary: Ark is the protocol this wallet runs on: a second layer on bitcoin for instant, cheap, self-custodial payments.
terms.definition: The Ark protocol is a second layer on the bitcoin network. It offers: simple boarding, low and predictable fees, instant payments, Lightning interoperability, and full control over your bitcoin.

terms.summary: A central server that coordinates rounds, helps with boarding and offboarding, deploys liquidity, and enables users to transact over the Lightning Network.
terms.definition: A central server that coordinates rounds, helps with boarding and offboarding, deploys liquidity, and enables users to transact over the Lightning Network. The Ark server does not custody any user bitcoin.

terms.summary: A VTXO is a coin on Ark: your Ark balance is made of VTXOs, and each one has a limited lifetime.
terms.definition: Short for "virtual unspent transaction output" or "virtual UTXO". A series of off-chain, pre-signed transactions that a user can broadcast at any time to retrieve their bitcoin on-chain in an emergency. VTXOs have a limited lifetime and must be refreshed periodically.

terms.summary: An arkoor payment is an instant Ark-to-Ark payment, made without waiting for a round.
terms.definition: Short for "Ark out-of-round"—the method used for Ark payments. Arkoor transactions create spend VTXOs.

terms.summary: Boarding moves on-chain bitcoin into Ark; it becomes spendable once the board transaction confirms.
terms.definition: The process of getting bitcoin onto an Ark. A user co-signs a special type of funding transaction with the Ark server and broadcasts it. Once confirmed, the resulting transaction represents the creation of a new VTXO.

terms.summary: The on-chain funding transaction created when a user boards onto Ark.
terms.definition: The on-chain funding transaction created when a user boards onto Ark. Once confirmed, it serves as the chain anchor for the resulting VTXO.

terms.summary: Board VTXOs are created when users first move bitcoin onto Ark, representing the simplest VTXO construction.
terms.definition: Board VTXOs are created when users first move bitcoin onto Ark, representing the simplest VTXO construction.

terms.summary: Offboarding is the normal way out: the Ark server cooperates and pays the amount to an on-chain address.
terms.definition: The standard, cooperative process of withdrawing bitcoin from Ark. A user forfeits one or more VTXOs and receives an output for the same amount on-chain.

terms.summary: A refresh swaps VTXOs for new ones in a round before they expire; the wallet usually does it for you.
terms.definition: The process of forfeiting old VTXOs for new ones during an Ark round, before their lifetime ends. The wallet app participates interactively during the round, signing its own exit branches in the transaction tree. See also delegated refresh for mobile devices that cannot reliably wake during scheduled rounds.

terms.summary: Refresh VTXOs are created during Ark server rounds when users must refresh expiring VTXOs or when they want to improve security after receiving spend VTXOs.
terms.definition: Refresh VTXOs are created during Ark server rounds when users must refresh expiring VTXOs or when they want to improve security after receiving spend VTXOs.

terms.summary: Spend VTXOs are created instantly when users send payments within the same Ark server, using a technique known as arkoor (Ark out-of-round).
terms.definition: Spend VTXOs are created instantly when users send payments within the same Ark server, using a technique known as arkoor (Ark out-of-round).

terms.summary: A periodic event initiated by the Ark server where users can refresh their VTXOs.
terms.definition: A periodic event initiated by the Ark server where users can refresh their VTXOs. Only users participating in the refresh have their VTXOs included in the round transaction.

terms.summary: The root transaction of a transaction tree that is broadcast on-chain during an Ark round.
terms.definition: The root transaction of a transaction tree that is broadcast on-chain during an Ark round. This transaction provides users with verifiable assurance that they can unilaterally retrieve their bitcoin on-chain.

terms.summary: A term used for VTXOs that are included in the transaction tree embedded in the round transaction.
terms.definition: A term used for VTXOs that are included in the transaction tree embedded in the round transaction. All refreshed VTXOs are in-round.

terms.summary: VTXOs expire, after 28 days on Second's server, so they have to be refreshed or spent before then.
terms.definition: The time limit set on VTXOs that requires users to spend or refresh their VTXOs before they expire. Once a VTXO expires, the Ark server can sweep the bitcoin on-chain and an emergency exit is no longer possible. The user can still refresh the VTXO, offboard it, or send it over Lightning with the server's cooperation, but can't send it as an Ark payment. On Second's Ark server, a standard VTXO lifetime is 28 days (server-configurable parameter).

terms.summary: An emergency exit takes bitcoin on-chain without the server's help: slow and paid for in on-chain fees, but always possible.
terms.definition: The non-standard, non-cooperative process of withdrawing bitcoin from Ark. The user independently broadcasts each off-chain transaction from their VTXO in sequence, until the bitcoin is delivered to an address they solely control. The availability of emergency exits guarantees that users maintain self-custody of their bitcoin. Sometimes shortened to "exit".

terms.summary: A transaction that releases a user's bitcoin on-chain, at the leaf of a transaction tree.
terms.definition: A transaction that releases a user's bitcoin on-chain, at the leaf of a transaction tree. Used when a user wants to retrieve their bitcoin from the Ark protocol.

terms.summary: Sweeps all claimable exit outputs into a single on-chain transaction sent to the specified address.
terms.definition: Sweeps all claimable exit outputs into a single on-chain transaction sent to the specified address.

terms.summary: An attempt by a user to broadcast VTXO transactions on-chain (initiate an emergency exit) after forfeiting them.
terms.definition: An attempt by a user to broadcast VTXO transactions on-chain (initiate an emergency exit) after forfeiting them. Should always fail due to timelocks securing exits.

terms.summary: A transaction that allows a user to give up ownership of their VTXO.
terms.definition: A transaction that allows a user to give up ownership of their VTXO. It uses one of the two spending paths in an exit transaction and grants all bitcoin to the Ark server. Used in refreshes and offboards.

terms.summary: A mechanism that ensures forfeit transactions are only valid if a specific on-chain payment is broadcast.
terms.definition: A mechanism that ensures forfeit transactions are only valid if a specific on-chain payment is broadcast. Used in on-chain payments and offboards. For rounds, connectors have been replaced by hash-locks.

terms.summary: A lock that releases bitcoin to whoever reveals the preimage of a hash.
terms.definition: A lock that releases bitcoin to whoever reveals the preimage of a hash. In Second's Ark, hash-locks replaced connectors in rounds (hArk).

terms.summary: The on-chain transaction output that a VTXO's validity depends on.
terms.definition: The on-chain transaction output that a VTXO's validity depends on. For in-round VTXOs this is an output of the round transaction; for boarded VTXOs it is an output of the board transaction. The chain anchor must be confirmed on-chain for the VTXO to be spendable.

terms.summary: A hierarchical structure of transactions that enables UTXO-sharing.
terms.definition: A hierarchical structure of transactions that enables UTXO-sharing. It consists of a root transaction (broadcast on-chain), branch transactions, and leaf transactions, allowing multiple users to share a single on-chain UTXO while maintaining control of their bitcoin.

terms.summary: The number of transactions a user must broadcast to complete an emergency exit.
terms.definition: The number of transactions a user must broadcast to complete an emergency exit. For a refresh VTXO, this is determined by the number of branch layers in the tree, which scales logarithmically with the number of users in the round. Each spend VTXO in a chain adds to the exit length.

terms.summary: A series of interdependent, off-chain transactions that break up the round transaction into successively smaller chunks until a user's Ark balance is released.
terms.definition: A series of interdependent, off-chain transactions that break up the round transaction into successively smaller chunks until a user's Ark balance is released. Each branch transaction can only be broadcast after the preceding branch transaction has been broadcast.

terms.summary: The final transaction in a branch, releasing a user's bitcoin on-chain.
terms.definition: The final transaction in a branch, releasing a user's bitcoin on-chain. See exit transaction.

terms.summary: The single on-chain transaction that all associated branch and leaf transactions emanate from.
terms.definition: The single on-chain transaction that all associated branch and leaf transactions emanate from. For in-round VTXOs, this is the round transaction; for boarded VTXOs, it is the board transaction. See chain anchor.

terms.summary: The process by which the Ark server transfers all remaining bitcoin from an expired round to its operational wallet, including the bitcoin in VTXOs their owners never refreshed.
terms.definition: The process by which the Ark server transfers all remaining bitcoin from an expired round to its operational wallet, including the bitcoin in VTXOs their owners never refreshed. Usually requires only a single on-chain transaction, because the whole round still sits in one output of the round transaction. If any user in the round has started or completed an emergency exit, the broadcast branch transactions split the round's bitcoin across more on-chain outputs. The server must then sweep more outputs and pay more in on-chain fees.

terms.summary: Refreshing VTXOs by having designated co-signers sign on the user's behalf, designed for mobile devices that cannot reliably wake during scheduled round windows.
terms.definition: Refreshing VTXOs by having designated co-signers sign on the user's behalf, designed for mobile devices that cannot reliably wake during scheduled round windows. Requires trusting that at least one designated co-signer behaves honestly.

terms.summary: Short for "Hash-lock Ark"—a protocol enhancement introduced in January 2026 that enables delegated refreshes for mobile devices and streamlines the refresh process.
terms.definition: Short for "Hash-lock Ark"—a protocol enhancement introduced in January 2026 that enables delegated refreshes for mobile devices and streamlines the refresh process.

terms.summary: Short for "covenant-less Ark"—an implementation variant that uses recursive multisigs instead of CTV covenants.
terms.definition: Short for "covenant-less Ark"—an implementation variant that uses recursive multisigs instead of CTV covenants. Each node policy contains a multisig with all the public keys of all the leaves below it, plus the server key.

terms.summary: A Lightning node connected to the Ark server that enables users to transact with the broader Lightning Network and users on other Ark servers.
terms.definition: A Lightning node connected to the Ark server that enables users to transact with the broader Lightning Network and users on other Ark servers.

terms.summary: A wallet-level operation that changes the state of one or more VTXOs—such as a round participation, arkoor payment, board, offboard, exit, or Lightning send/receive.
terms.definition: A wallet-level operation that changes the state of one or more VTXOs—such as a round participation, arkoor payment, board, offboard, exit, or Lightning send/receive. A movement is created when the operation starts, locks any affected VTXOs while in progress, and transitions to a final status (successful, failed, or canceled) when the operation completes.

terms.summary: Every Bark wallet posts a record of its VTXOs to a mailbox on the Ark server that only its mnemonic can unlock.
terms.definition: Every Bark wallet posts a record of its VTXOs to a mailbox on the Ark server that only its mnemonic can unlock.

terms.summary: Ark servers deploy bitcoin upfront for refreshes, on-chain payments, and Lightning payments.
terms.definition: Ark servers deploy bitcoin upfront for refreshes, on-chain payments, and Lightning payments.

terms.summary: An address for receiving Ark payments.
terms.definition: An address for receiving Ark payments. Mainnet ones start ark1, signet ones tark1. Too long to read aloud: show it as a QR.

terms.summary: A tiny output anyone can spend to raise a transaction's fee with CPFP.
terms.definition: A tiny output anyone can spend to raise a transaction's fee with CPFP. Bark uses it to make emergency exits cheaper.

terms.summary: What you can pay out over Lightning or Ark.
terms.definition: What you can pay out over Lightning or Ark.

terms.summary: An on-chain deposit boarding onto Ark.
terms.definition: An on-chain deposit boarding onto Ark.

terms.definition: Bitcoin in a refresh that hasn't completed yet.

terms.definition: An outgoing Lightning payment that hasn't settled yet.

terms.definition: A Lightning payment Barkd has yet to claim.

terms.definition: Bitcoin pending the completion of an emergency exit.

terms.definition: An incoming on-chain payment awaiting confirmation.

terms.definition: Change from emergency exit fee transactions, awaiting confirmation.

terms.definition: Build a self-custodial wallet app for mobile, desktop, or the browser: a Rust core with TypeScript, Flutter, Swift, Kotlin, and Go bindings.

terms.definition: Second's MCP server for a Bark wallet: the wallet tools, spend caps and mainnet opt-in that bark-voice builds on.

terms.summary: Bitcoin's network of payment channels.
terms.definition: Bitcoin's network of payment channels. An Ark wallet pays and gets paid over Lightning through the Ark server's Lightning gateway.

terms.summary: The standard Lightning invoice: a one-time payment request, usually for a fixed amount.
terms.definition: The standard Lightning invoice: a one-time payment request, usually for a fixed amount.

terms.definition: A reusable Lightning payment request, called an offer: it can be paid many times.

terms.definition: An email-style address (name@domain) that a wallet turns into a Lightning invoice. Paying one always needs an amount.

terms.definition: A family of Lightning links (pay, withdraw, login) that a wallet follows to get an invoice or a payment.

terms.definition: A payment that unlocks with a secret (the preimage) before a deadline, or returns to the sender after it. Lightning payments are chains of HTLCs.

terms.summary: The secret that proves a Lightning payment was made: whoever reveals it gets paid.
terms.definition: The secret that proves a Lightning payment was made: whoever reveals it gets paid.

terms.summary: The hash of a payment's preimage.
terms.definition: The hash of a payment's preimage. An invoice carries it; the payment settles when the preimage is revealed.

terms.summary: Paying for an API or web resource with Lightning: the server answers 402 Payment Required with an invoice, and the paid preimage unlocks it.
terms.definition: Paying for an API or web resource with Lightning: the server answers 402 Payment Required with an invoice, and the paid preimage unlocks it.

terms.definition: Recorded in a bitcoin block. On-chain payments are final once confirmed, but slower and costlier than Ark or Lightning.

terms.definition: Held or paid without a transaction in a block, as on Ark and Lightning.

terms.definition: A block that includes a transaction (and each block after it). More confirmations, more final.

terms.definition: What a transaction pays per unit of size, in sats per virtual byte (sat/vB). Higher confirms sooner.
